report.summary: Chunk 3 of graph_delta.py: implements mutation sensitivity analysis, specificity analysis via real commits, and per-function reference delta for defect detection calibration.
risks: commit_shas | low | Uses _git which may return None; splitlines on None could raise AttributeError if out is None. | Check if _git can return None and handle it before splitlines.
measure_commit | medium | _git('show', f'{sha}^:{rel}') may fail for root commit (parent does not exist). The code does not handle that case. | Verify behavior for root commits and add handling.

function_deltas | medium | Functions with same name in different classes are conflated; qualifier uses only node.name without class scope. | Check if the function names are unique across classes; if not, add qualifier.
specificity | low | If rows list is empty, used list is empty, division by zero not possible but metrics may be misleading. | Ensure edge case of empty used list is handled.

measure_commit | medium | max_files bound silently skips commits; the skipped reason is recorded but the commit is excluded from stats. That is a design choice but could bias results. | Confirm that the bound is appropriate and documented.

handoff.purpose: Implements mutation sensitivity analysis, specificity measurement via real commits, and per-function reference delta computation.

symbols.name: _int_arg
symbols.note: Parses an integer from argv at flag position, returns default on failure.

symbols.name: _git
symbols.note: Runs a git command in repo_root, returns stdout or None on non-zero return.

symbols.name: commit_shas
symbols.note: Returns list of non-merge commit SHAs touching Python files, newest first.

symbols.name: measure_commit
symbols.note: Computes layer deltas (added, removed, type_moved) for a single real commit.

symbols.name: specificity
symbols.note: Runs specificity analysis on real commits, returns stats including pure deletions.

symbols.name: _refs_by_function
symbols.note: Returns per-function reference multisets from AST, excluding docstrings.

symbols.name: function_deltas
symbols.note: Returns per-function added/removed reference counts for functions present in both versions.

claims.text: An unparsable half is not a detection and not a failure of the detector; counting it either way would move the headline for a bookkeeping reason.
claims.why: The code catches SyntaxError, ValueError, RecursionError and continues the loop without incrementing row['detected'] or row['n']. It does not count the mutant as detected or even as a valid mutant for the operator row, so the claim is accurate.

claims.text: ``--limit 40``, or the default. Silent fallback is deliberate: a malformed limit should not lose the run, and the value is echoed in the written report either way.
claims.why: The function tries to index argv after the flag; if flag not found or index+1 out of range, it returns default without raising. The value is indeed echoed in the report via the caller's usage.

claims.text: The mutation corpus contains only BAD patches, so it measures sensitivity and cannot measure specificity at all. A signal that moves for every change discriminates nothing. This arm runs REAL COMMITS through the identical pipeline so the two distributions can be compared.
claims.why: This claim refers to the overall design rationale and the existence of a separate mutation corpus not present in this chunk. The code does implement the 'specificity arm' but the claim about the mutation corpus is not checkable here.

claims.text: five of the seven detected mutations were PURE DELETIONS (``+0/-N``). Seeded defects disable things — they remove a guard, a call, a check — while real work usually adds or exchanges.
claims.why: This claim references prior results from mutation analysis not included in this chunk. The code does compute pure_deletion in measure_commit but the specific numbers are not checkable.

claims.text: Non-merge commits touching Python, newest first. Merges are excluded because a merge's diff against its first parent attributes other people's work to it, which would pollute the corpus with changes it did not make.
claims.why: The function uses '--no-merges' flag and '--', '*.py' to filter Python files. The format includes '%H' for full SHA. Newest first is default git log order. The rationale is stated but not enforced by code beyond the flags.

claims.text: The same layer delta, for one real commit. Returns per-file and totals.
claims.why: The function computes added/removed/type_moved per file and aggregates totals, returns a dict with per_file list and summary fields.

claims.text: A sweeping commit would dominate the distribution for a reason that has nothing to do with defectiveness. Bounded and SAID, never silently cut.
claims.why: The code checks if len(files) > max_files and if so sets skipped reason and returns early. The commit is excluded from stats, and the reason is recorded in the skipped list.

claims.text: Per-FUNCTION reference multisets. The granularity a defect actually has. Aggregating a delta per commit was wrong... A seeded defect edits ONE function; so the comparison has to be one function wide or the signal drowns in the rest of the patch.
claims.why: The function extracts reference counts per function (FunctionDef and AsyncFunctionDef), excluding docstrings. It returns a dict keyed by function name. The rationale is explanatory, and the implementation matches the description.

claims.text: One row per function that exists in BOTH versions and changed. Functions added or removed wholesale are excluded: a new function has no 'before' to lose references against, and counting it as a huge addition would swamp the distribution the rule is read from.
claims.why: The function computes the intersection of function names from before and after, iterates over those, and only includes rows where added or removed > 0. Functions only in one version are ignored.

observations.what: The mutation sensitivity loop catches SyntaxError, ValueError, RecursionError and continues without recording the mutant in the operator row. This means the operator's n is not incremented for unparseable mutants, which could undercount the total mutants per operator.

In measure_commit, the _git call for the parent version uses f'{sha}^:{rel}'. For the root commit (no parent), this will fail and return None, causing 'before' to be set to '' (empty string) because of the check 'if before is None: before = ""'. However, the _git call may also fail for other reasons, and the code does not distinguish between 'file not found in parent' and 'git error'. It treats any None as 'added in this commit', which could be incorrect if git fails for other reasons.

_refs_by_function qualifies function names by line number only via the comment: 'Qualify by line so two same-named methods in one file stay distinct.' However, the actual code does not implement line qualification; it uses f"{node.name}" without line number. The comment is misleading.
In function_deltas, functions with the same name in different classes are conflated because the key is just the function name. The code does not include class scope.

The specificity function returns 'rows' which is a list of all used commit results. This list can be large (up to limit) and is included in the return value. The caller may need to handle large output.
